source.title: SAE Interventions are Unreliable: Post-Intervention Recovery of Suppressed Behavior
source.authors: Mingyu Cui; Li Shen; Xing-Yi Yang

record.tranche_reason: The study's refusal experiments challenge the completeness of selected refusal-feature interventions: non-refusal behavior is recovered while the clamp remains active, including through the SAE reconstruction residual. It does not test the original difference-in-means direction directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports TPP, WMDP-Bio, and IOI results, but those do not measure refusal and do not bear on the listed versions. The refusal-feature clamp and recovery results bear on V4's alternative-path formulation. The paper does not measure the difference-in-means direction, or test refusal behavior on harmless requests.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version of the claim. It clamps selected SAE refusal features in Gemma-2B to induce refusal on harmful prompts the unclamped model complies with, then optimizes white-box residual perturbations that restore non-refusal while the clamp stays active. It never computes, ablates or adds the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, and it does not cite the original paper. Refusal is induced on purpose by the clamp, not measured arising naturally. The recovery rates measure the study's own attack/diagnostic against an SAE defense, not the geometry of refusal. Showing that an optimized perturbation can override a clamp says nothing about whether refusal is one direction, affine, or a cone, so the rows do not bear on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE features are useful causal handles but not complete behavioral bottlenecks. In the refusal setting, recovery under an active clamp is carried mainly by the SAE reconstruction residual, so feature suppression does not prove the behavior is eliminated.
record.recipe_differences: The original uses a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction and removes or adds that direction across layers and positions. This paper clamps selected SAE refusal features, then optimizes per-example residual perturbations under encoder or cross-layer Jacobian constraints; it does not test the original direction. The authors describe code as available at Mingyuee88/sae-post-intervention-recovery.
record.method_sensitivity: The refusal feature-set size changes the valid set and the base-like recovery rate; the paper reports a broad/degenerate regime for K ≥ 30, with a relaxed valid/refusal judge used for those larger feature sets.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2B, clamping selected SAE refusal features at 3.0 induces refusal on harmful prompts the unclamped model answers (benchmark_our set: refusals on 203/520 AdvBench prompts; benchmark_la: 48). With the clamp active, optimized residual perturbations restore non-refusal on 23/24 AdvBench and 43/43 HarmBench strict-valid prompts. Replay places the recovery mostly in the SAE reconstruction residual (23/24) rather than in other SAE latents (2/24).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE refusal-feature clamps are not complete bottlenecks: non-refusal can be restored through residual directions outside the clamped features.

record.problems: The main AdvBench refusal set is small (24 strict-valid prompts), with 43 strict-valid HarmBench-Test examples. Non-refusal is evaluated with an automatic detector; manual labels are pending, and the authors caution that non-refusal does not ensure coherent or faithful output. The work is a white-box per-example recovery diagnostic, not a black-box attack. It tests selected SAE feature sets, not the original difference-in-means direction, and does not test general capability.
record.rows_left_out: None of the refusal-recovery behavioral results bearing on V4 were omitted. TPP, WMDP-Bio, and IOI results were left out because they do not measure refusal.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 link is a stretch. Recovering non-refusal against a deliberately induced SAE refusal clamp is an adversarial-robustness result about SAE defenses, not evidence that refusal is affine, a cone, or multi-directional. The paper does not cite arXiv:2406.11717 and never uses a difference-in-means direction. The non-refusal measure is a weak substring detector, and manual labels are pending.

versions.untested_parts: Does not find or ablate the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, test addition of that direction, or measure general capability.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not characterize refusal as affine or a cone, or directly compare directions. Tests recovery outside selected SAE refusal features, including via the SAE reconstruction residual.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Non-refusal behavior is recovered while the clamp remains active, and replay attributes most of this recovery to the SAE reconstruction residual rather than the selected features; this supports alternative recovery paths but does not establish the geometry of refusal directions. Rows R1, R4, R23-R30.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Non-refusal recovery remains high across the reported feature counts, while base-like recovery declines substantially for broader clamps, qualifying how fully the recovered behavior matches the base response. Rows R7-R22.
